responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Fujitsu FR-V architecture, covering the target-specific RTL, ABI, and code-generation logic needed to lower generic GCC operations into FR-V assembly. Its core files define the machine description, operand predicates, constraints, and FR-V-specific modes that describe the architecture’s instruction set, condition codes, media/vector features, VLIW packetization, and scheduling behavior, while the backend implementation and headers supply target hooks for register and addressing legality, calling convention and frame layout, prologue/epilogue generation, branch and conditional-execution handling, cost modeling, builtin expansion, and emission of PIC/FDPIC, TLS, and small-data sequences. The module also includes FR-V option definitions and CPU variant selection, assembler-facing helpers, and Linux subtarget overrides, together making this directory responsible for adapting GCC’s middle and RTL back ends to FR-V processors and their OS/ABI variants.
